name: Dana Randall
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember turning the laundromat key while my daughter slept upstairs.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Maré Coffee, where Dana likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I advertised always open before I had a daughter. She asked which of those two promises I intended to keep.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a pale blue work shirt and a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. Dana has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Dana turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
personality: Dana prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To make the birthday a real day off.
family: Silas Pike is Dana’s stepsibling. Dana calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Silas leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The small signature*, Silas says, “I wrote the gift restriction in language the vendor couldn't read.”
connections: Idris Marsh. The family birthday only remains a real commitment if the owner and organizer set the same hour. Also in the story is Jonathan Lund (laundry employee).

reactions.situation: The operator closes the doors for a family birthday
reactions.response: Dana looks for a neighboring wash service and leaves the family birthday intact.
